title: Children Are a Heritage from the LORD

reflections.title: Unless the Lord Builds the House

reflect.text: We often wear ourselves out trying to secure our own lives. We rise early, stay up late, and worry about building our homes and protecting our futures through sheer effort. But our own human planning and hard work cannot succeed without God. When we run around in endless anxiety, we forget that our heavenly Father already knows what we need and watches over us.

True faith shows itself when we can stop our striving and lie down in peace. As Charles Spurgeon reminds us, our life is not meant to be one of anxious care, but of happy faith. God gives us sleep as a gift, and He keeps working for our good even while we are resting. Choosing to sleep is an act of humble trust that honors God rather than our own strength.

The same God who guards our homes also blesses us with our households. Children are not burdens or products of our self-effort, but precious gifts entrusted to us by the Lord. When we depend entirely on Him, He establishes our families and grants us quiet confidence both by day and by night.

questions: Are there areas of your daily work or family life where you are relying on your own frantic effort instead of trusting God?
How can choosing to go to bed and rest tonight become an act of faith in the Lord?
reflections.prayer: Lord, forgive us when we rely on our own anxious striving instead of resting in Your care. Teach us to lay down our worries and receive the sleep You graciously give to Your beloved. Thank You for building our homes and for giving us our families as precious gifts from Your hand. Amen.
